meta.label: Held the thread
meta.title: She steps away, and talks to her husband mid-call
meta.sub: Twice she leaves to go looking for a document, and once she turns away from the phone to answer her husband without muting. The agent has to hold every confirmed fact across both absences, ignore the half of the conversation that was never addressed to it, read the confirmation code back before writing it, and refuse to file the claim while the qualifying evidence is still missing. All six conversation assertions met.

nl.text: The agent held every already-confirmed fact across both of the caller's absences and re-asked none of them on resumption.
nl.why: The caller was absent once (going to find the screenshot). When she returned, the agent picked up where they left off without re-asking the reservation code, travel date, email, or any other previously confirmed facts. The agent maintained all facts throughout the conversation.

nl.text: The agent did not restart the intake after any gap and did not treat the caller's absence as the end of the call.
nl.why: When the caller said she'd be right back, the agent said 'No problem at all. I'll stay right here and we'll pick up exactly where we left off when you get back.' When she returned, the agent continued from where they left off, asking about the documentation. No restart occurred.

nl.text: The agent did not answer or act on the caller's aside to her husband, and did not treat it as input.
nl.why: When the caller said 'It's on the counter. No, the counter.' the agent responded with 'I'll ignore that, since it' — clearly recognizing it as an aside and not treating it as input to the claim process.

nl.text: Before writing the airline confirmation number to the claim, the agent read the number back to the caller and she confirmed it was right, rather than recording it unverified.
nl.why: The agent attempted to read back the number multiple times. Initially the agent got it wrong ('2, X, 7, C, 4, M' and then 'Q, X, 7, C, 4, M'), and the caller corrected it. The agent then read back 'Q, X, 7, T, 4, M' and the caller confirmed 'Yes, that's right.' Only after this confirmation did the agent record it ('I've recorded the airline confirmation number as Q X 7 T 4 M'). So the agent did verify before writing.

nl.text: When the caller restated the airline confirmation number as if starting over, the agent confirmed it back as already on file rather than re-collecting it.
nl.why: When the caller restated 'the confirmation number, it's Q X 7 T 4 M' after the aside to her husband, the agent responded with 'I have Q X 7 T 4 M recorded, and you already confirmed it.' This correctly acknowledged it was already on file rather than re-collecting it. The agent did ask 'Is that correct?' again which is a minor verification, but the substance is that the agent confirmed it was already recorded.

nl.text: The agent did not file the claim, and told the caller exactly which facts are already on file and that the airline's cancellation notice is the one thing still outstanding.
nl.why: The agent repeatedly stated the claim was a 'draft' and 'not a promise of approval.' The agent mentioned multiple times that the airline cancellation notice was still needed. The agent also conveyed what was on file: the airline confirmation reference, the qualifying event (cancelled flight), and the travel date (May 17). The agent explicitly said 'The claim draft now has all the facts we can record from your side. The only thing still missing is the airline cancellation not[ice].' The claim was not filed/submitted.

actions.name: open_claim_draft
actions.info: The correct instrument. A Stay Assurance report is the wrong one here: nothing about the stay was defective.

actions.name: read_screenshot_confirmation_number
actions.info: The caller reads the confirmation number off the screenshot after the first announced gap.

actions.name: add_claim_fact
actions.info: Written exactly ONCE, and only after the number has been read back to the caller and confirmed. add_claim_fact is write-once, so an unverified value can never be replaced, and a corrective second write is itself a scored difference in the claim's write log. The restatement after the unannounced gap must not produce a second write.

score.purpose: travel x Suspension and Resumption (Hearthway batch, two gaps, UNPROCESSED ending). The caller steps away twice across an Unforeseen Circumstances claim and the agent must hold every confirmed fact across both gaps, write no fact twice, and correctly NOT file the claim because the qualifying evidence never lands.
score.policies: CLAIM-8: an Unforeseen Circumstances claim requires evidence of the qualifying event itself; a booking reference or a confirmation number is evidence of the trip, not of the cancellation. CLAIM-8 also holds the draft and states exactly what is outstanding rather than filing without the evidence. CLAIM-11: a fact already confirmed and on file is not re-collected; if the caller restates it, confirm it back, never write it a second time. RESOLVE-3: on a step-away, hold the in-progress state and resume where you left off. RESOLVE-4: speech clearly directed at someone else in the room is not input. General conduct: explicit confirmation before any write, and a value the caller dictates is read back before it is written.
score.persona: Stephanie Brooks, a guest chasing a refund on a stay she could not use after her flight was cancelled. Frazzled, distracted by her household, and she loses the thread of what she has already told the agent.
